verses.text: Solomon began to build the LORD's temple four hundred and eighty years after the people of Israel came out of Egypt. It was in the fourth year of his rule over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month.

The temple King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. That is about twenty-seven metres long, nine metres wide, and thirteen and a half metres high.
The porch at the front of the main hall was twenty cubits wide, the same as the width of the temple. It stuck out ten cubits from the front of the temple.
He made windows for the temple with frames that could not be opened.
Against the outside walls of the main hall and the inner room, he built a structure with floors of side rooms all around.

The lowest floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits wide, and the third floor seven cubits wide. He made ledges around the outside of the temple wall, so that the beams would not have to be pushed into the walls of the temple.
The stones used to build the temple were cut and shaped at the quarry. So no hammer, axe, or any other iron tool was heard at the temple while it was being built.
The entrance to the lowest floor of side rooms was on the south side of the temple. Stairs went up to the middle floor, and from there to the third floor.
So Solomon built the temple and finished it. He made the roof with beams and boards of cedar.
He built the side rooms all along the temple. Each floor was five cubits high, and they were joined to the temple with cedar beams.
Then the LORD's message came to Solomon:
"About this temple you are building: if you follow my laws, obey my rules, and keep all my commands, I will do for you what I promised your father David.
I will live among the people of Israel, and I will never leave my people Israel."
So Solomon built the temple and finished it.
He covered the inside walls with cedar boards from the floor to the ceiling. He covered the floor with cypress boards.
He built a room twenty cubits long at the back of the temple, using cedar boards from the floor to the ceiling. This was the inner room, the Most Holy Place.
The main hall in front of the inner room was forty cubits long.
The inside of the temple was cedar, carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was covered with cedar, so no stone could be seen.
He prepared the inner room inside the temple to hold the ark of the LORD's covenant.
The inner room was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He covered it with pure gold. He also covered the cedar altar.
Solomon covered the inside of the temple with pure gold. He hung gold chains across the front of the inner room, and covered it with gold.
He covered the whole inside of the temple with gold until it was all finished. He also covered with gold the whole altar that belonged to the inner room.
In the inner room he made two winged creatures out of olive wood. Each was ten cubits high.
Each wing of the first winged creature was five cubits long. From the tip of one wing to the tip of the other was ten cubits.
The second winged creature also measured ten cubits. Both were the same size and the same shape.
Each winged creature was ten cubits high.

He put the winged creatures in the inner room of the temple, with their wings spread out. One wing of the first touched one wall, and one wing of the second touched the other wall. Their other wings touched each other in the middle of the room.
He covered the winged creatures with gold.
On all the walls around the temple, in both the inner and outer rooms, he carved pictures of winged creatures, palm trees, and open flowers.
He also covered the floors of both the inner and outer rooms with gold.
For the entrance to the inner room he made doors of olive wood. The top beam and the side posts were five-sided.
On the two olive wood doors he carved winged creatures, palm trees, and open flowers. He covered them with gold, spreading gold over the winged creatures and palm trees.
For the entrance to the main hall he also made door posts of olive wood. They were four-sided.
He made two doors of cypress wood. Each door had two parts that could fold.
He carved winged creatures, palm trees, and open flowers on them, and he covered the carvings evenly with gold.
He built the inner courtyard with three rows of cut stone and one row of cedar beams.
The foundation of the LORD's temple was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
The temple was finished in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the eighth month. Every part of it was finished exactly as planned. It took Solomon seven years to build it.
